name: now.vulnerable/mcp
title: vulnerable.now
description: Free CVE lookups, package checks and patch priorities from public sources. No account or API key.

tools.name: get_vulnerability
tools.description: Get the merged entry for one or more IDs: CVE, GitHub advisory (GHSA), EUVD, or an OSV ID such as PYSEC, GO or RUSTSEC. Returns the description, CVSS, CISA KEV status, EPSS, public exploits, affected packages, fixed versions, priority and source links.

id.description: One ID, such as CVE-2021-44228, GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q or PYSEC-2021-19.

ids.description: Up to 20 IDs at once, for triaging scanner output.

tools.name: get_poc
tools.description: List the public exploit code and proofs of concept the sources link to one vulnerability: Metasploit exploit modules, Exploit-DB entries, references NVD or the CNA tagged as exploits (broken links left out), and GitHub PoC repositories (most stars first). Links only; nothing is downloaded or run. The same JSON as GET /api/v1/entries/{id}/pocs. GitHub PoCs and tagged references are unverified third-party code, and stars are popularity, not review.

id.description: A CVE, GHSA, EUVD or OSV ID, such as CVE-2021-44228.

sources.description: Only these sources. All by default.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Get the stored AI-written overview of one CVE: one paragraph on what the flaw is, what it affects, what an attacker can do, whether it is exploited and how to fix it, written by Hinoki Offensive One from the entry's source data. Overviews are written only when someone opens the CVE page on vulnerable.now, so this tool reads and never writes one. status says whether the paragraph is ready, stale (the sources changed since), missing or still being written. AI text can be wrong; check get_vulnerability and the sources. The same JSON as GET /api/v1/entries/{id}/overview.

id.description: A CVE ID, such as CVE-2024-3400. GHSA, EUVD and OSV IDs resolve to their CVE when it has one.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the whole catalog by words: product, vendor, package, CVE ID, common vulnerability name, research metadata or description text. Best match first by default. Each result says which fields matched. When nothing matches, the reply suggests a broader query.

q.description: Words to search for, such as "openssl", "log4j rce" or "exchange server".

kev.description: Only entries in the CISA KEV catalog.

exploited.description: Only entries with reported exploitation (KEV, CISA SSVC, ENISA, VulnCheck KEV or Shadowserver honeypots).

public_exploit.description: Only entries with public exploit code.

fix_available.description: Only entries with a fixed version.

type.description: Filter to CVEs or advisories without a CVE.

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem, such as npm, PyPI, Maven, Go or crates.io.

vendor.description: Exact vendor name, such as apache or microsoft.

product.description: Exact product name, such as log4j or exchange server.

package.description: Only entries naming this package, as ecosystem:name, such as npm:lodash or pypi:django.

tech.description: Only entries naming this vendor or vendor product, as a slug: apache, or apache/tomcat.

wordpress.description: Only entries naming this WordPress software. Use plugin:contact-form-7, theme:astra or core.

since.description: Only entries published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

until.description: Only entries published before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

modified_since.description: Only entries whose merged record changed at or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD) or time (ISO 8601). Pass the newest modified value from the previous run.

tools.name: get_package
tools.description: Every known vulnerability in one open source package, most urgent first, with the affected ranges and fixed versions published for that package. Give a version to learn which advisories affect it and the lowest upgrade that leaves every affecting range.

ecosystem.description: npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, RubyGems, Packagist, NuGet, Hex or Pub.

name.description: The package name, such as lodash, django, org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core or golang.org/x/net.

version.description: Optional exact version to check, such as 4.17.20.

only_affected.description: With version, list only the advisories that affect it.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Look up a vendor product such as an operating system, browser, server or appliance. With only a product name, returns a clear match or lists candidates. Give a version to see affected entries and the lowest upgrade that clears them. For WordPress core, plugins or themes, use get_wordpress.

product.description: The product name, such as WordPress, nginx, Tomcat or FortiOS.

vendor.description: Optional vendor name, such as Apache or Fortinet.

version.description: Optional exact version to check, such as 6.4.2.

only_affected.description: With version, list only the entries that affect it.

tools.name: list_feed
tools.description: Follow new or changed catalog entries. Defaults to newest first, or newest CISA KEV additions when kev is true. For incremental sync, pass modified_since with sort=modified. Use search for best matches to a text query.

kev.description: Only entries in the CISA KEV catalog.

exploited.description: Only entries with reported exploitation (KEV, CISA SSVC, ENISA, VulnCheck KEV or Shadowserver honeypots).

public_exploit.description: Only entries with public exploit code.

fix_available.description: Only entries with a fixed version.

type.description: Filter to CVEs or advisories without a CVE.

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem, such as npm, PyPI, Maven, Go or crates.io.

vendor.description: Exact vendor name, such as apache or microsoft.

product.description: Exact product name, such as log4j or exchange server.

package.description: Only entries naming this package, as ecosystem:name, such as npm:lodash or pypi:django.

tech.description: Only entries naming this vendor or vendor product, as a slug: apache, or apache/tomcat.

wordpress.description: Only entries naming this WordPress software. Use plugin:contact-form-7, theme:astra or core.

since.description: Only entries published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

until.description: Only entries published before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

modified_since.description: Only entries whose merged record changed at or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD) or time (ISO 8601). Pass the newest modified value from the previous run.

query.description: Words to match against IDs, titles, vendors, products and descriptions.

sort.description: Defaults to kev if kev is true, otherwise published.

tools.name: top_priority
tools.description: What to patch first: the vulnerabilities with the highest priority score (exploitation, EPSS, CVSS, automatability) among those with activity in a time window, optionally narrowed to an ecosystem, vendor or product.

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem, such as npm, PyPI, Maven, Go or crates.io.

vendor.description: Exact vendor name, such as apache or microsoft.

product.description: Exact product name, such as log4j or exchange server.

kev.description: Only entries in the CISA KEV catalog.

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Find known vulnerabilities in package versions and website technologies, ranked by what to fix first. Send a version list, lockfile, CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM, or Wappalyzer export. For a WordPress inventory of core, plugins and themes, use check_wordpress.

ecosystem.description: npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, RubyGems, Packagist, NuGet, Hex or Pub.

version.description: One exact version, not a range.

file.description: A whole file: a lockfile (recognized by its name), a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM, or a Wappalyzer JSON or CSV export. Up to 5 MB.

name.description: The file name, such as package-lock.json, bom.json or wappalyzer.csv.

technologies.description: Website technologies, as Wappalyzer or a person names them.

name.description: Such as nginx, PHP, WordPress or jQuery.

tools.name: get_wordpress
tools.description: Every known vulnerability in one WordPress plugin or theme, by its wordpress.org slug, or in WordPress core, most urgent first, with affected versions and fixes from Wordfence Intelligence and the CVE records. Without a slug, a name such as "Contact Form 7" is matched: a clear match is answered directly and otherwise the candidates are listed. Give a version to learn which entries affect it and the lowest upgrade that clears them.

slug.description: The wordpress.org slug, such as contact-form-7. Not needed for core.

name.description: The plugin or theme name, when the slug is unknown.

version.description: Optional exact version to check, such as 5.8.1.

only_affected.description: With version, list only the entries that affect it.

tools.name: check_wordpress
tools.description: Check every version a WordPress site runs: the core version and its plugins and themes, as {slug, version} lists or the raw output of wp plugin list and wp theme list (table, CSV or JSON). Returns, most urgent first, which installed versions are affected, by which entries, and what to update to. Plugins with no public records are reported as not in the catalog. Nothing is fetched from the site.

core.description: The WordPress version, such as 6.8.3 (wp core version).

plugins.description: Plugins as [{"slug", "version"}], or WP-CLI output or one "slug version" per line as a string.

themes.description: Themes, in the same forms as plugins.
